title: A tower with injective levels and split transitions is injective
statement: Let $I=(I_n,p_n)_{n\geq1}$ be an inverse system [def-weil-inverse-system] of abelian groups in the tower category [lem-pc-tower-abelian]. If every $I_n$ is an injective abelian group [def-sp-injective-resolutions] and every transition map $p_n:I_{n+1}\to I_n$ is a split surjection, then $I$ is an injective object [def-sp-injective-resolutions] of the abelian tower category [lem-pc-tower-abelian].

source.place: Tag 07KW, Lemma 15.88.1 proof footnote (the compatible lifting argument after the split-tower construction)

proof.text: To verify injectivity [def-sp-injective-resolutions], let $\iota:A\hookrightarrow B$ be a monomorphism of towers, with transition maps $f_n:A_{n+1}\to A_n$ and $g_n:B_{n+1}\to B_n$, and let $\varphi:A\to I$ be a tower morphism [def-weil-inverse-system]. Each $\iota_n:A_n\to B_n$ is injective: given $a\in A_n$ with $\iota_n(a)=0$, let $T$ be the tower with $T_m=\mathbf Z$ for $m\leq n$, $T_m=0$ for $m>n$, identity transitions below level $n$ and zero transitions above. A tower morphism $T\to A$ is the same as an element of $A_n$ (its level-$m$ component for $m\leq n$ sends $1$ to the image of that element under the composite transition $A_n\to A_m$), and composition is componentwise, so $\iota\circ\alpha=\iota\circ0$ for the morphism $\alpha$ determined by $a$; as $\iota$ is a monomorphism, $\alpha=0$, i.e. $a=0$. Start by extending $\varphi_1:A_1\to I_1$ to $\psi_1:B_1\to I_1$, using injectivity of the abelian group $I_1$.

source.place: Tag 07KW, Lemma 15.88.1 proof footnote (the compatible lifting argument after the split-tower construction)

proof.text: Inductively suppose $\psi_n:B_n\to I_n$ extends $\varphi_n$ and satisfies $p_{n-1}\psi_n=\psi_{n-1}g_{n-1}$. Choose a section $s_n:I_n\to I_{n+1}$ of the split epimorphism $p_n$. On $A_{n+1}$ define $d=\varphi_{n+1}-s_n\psi_ng_n$; since $\psi_n g_n=\varphi_n f_n$ there, $p_n d=\varphi_nf_n-\varphi_nf_n=0$, so $d$ lands in $K=\ker p_n$. The splitting gives $I_{n+1}\cong K\oplus I_n$, hence $K$ is injective: extend a map into $I_{n+1}$ and project to the $K$ summand (equivalently, extend into the direct summand). Extend $d$ along $A_{n+1}\hookrightarrow B_{n+1}$ to $\chi:B_{n+1}\to K$, and put $\psi_{n+1}=\chi+s_n\psi_ng_n$. It extends $\varphi_{n+1}$ and satisfies $p_n\psi_{n+1}=\psi_ng_n$. Induction produces a compatible tower morphism $\psi:B\to I$ extending $\varphi$, which is exactly injectivity of $I$ by [def-sp-injective-resolutions].
